sense: complete, utter: total silence, total nonsense

evidence: Cic. Agr. 1.21: summa tranquillitās pācis et ōtiī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 44: ex summā inopiā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The highest degree of anything: total calm, total want, the greatest difficulty.
Properly unmixed, as wine without water (merum); then “nothing but”: mera mōnstra nūntiārat, he had brought nothing but horrors (Cic. Att. 4.7.1).

phrases.latin: nōn homō sed lītus atque āēr et sōlitūdō mera
phrases.english: (of a man who was no company) not a man but a seashore, thin air, utter emptiness

phrases.latin: tanta repente vīlitās ex summā inopiā et cāritāte reī frūmentāriae cōnsecūta est
phrases.english: so sudden a fall in prices followed upon total scarcity and the dearness of grain

sources: Lewis & Short: summus · Lewis & Short: superus · Lewis & Short: merus
Cicero (Att. 1.18.1, 4.7.1, 9.13.8; Imp. Pomp. 44) and Caesar (BG 4.17) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
